statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window. Stress moves into the elevated band because the rate, energy and diplomatic questions behind it became less resolved, not because any drawdown was observed.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold for every published hour: no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, roughly eighteen hours beyond the final slot. headline: Nasdaq-100 holds inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail stays at its floor while a rejected Hormuz plan, a post-2007 long-end yield peak and $92 crude lift Stress into the elevated band
body:
Every Nasdaq-100 venue has been shut since the Friday 21:00Z settle, and the entire 24-hour published window closes eighteen hours before CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday. Friday's session itself was orderly and two-sided: cash NDX closed 30,608.14, up 129.28 points or 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, against a 30,478.86 previous close. NQ December 2026 futures settled 30,889.25, up 122.50 or 0.40%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range. All three major US averages posted weekly gains: the Dow rose 478.64 points or 0.93% to 51,828.62 and snapped a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not hold an extreme into the close, so none of the mean-reversion-failure amplifiers this contract requires were present when the tape stopped.

The cross-asset backdrop remains the reason Stress sits well above Tail. The 10-year Treasury closed at 5.18%, its highest since the global financial crisis, after printing 5.225% intraday, the highest since 2007, while the 30-year touched 5.502%, its highest since 2004; the Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.87% and the 10-year at 5.18% for its latest September 24 column. WTI November futures settled $92.41, down 2.33%, and Brent settled $104.32, down 2.14%. Index internals were dispersed rather than one-way: MSFT rose 3.66% to 516.17, its highest close this year, while META fell 3.33% to 751.66.

One material item has changed since the previous assessment. Friday's crude decline rested on optimism that Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days could be accepted; reporting now indicates that plan was rejected, with renewed strikes seen as likely only after the November midterm elections. That removes a near-term de-escalation path rather than creating immediate escalation, and Hormuz transits are reported near nine vessels, far below peacetime levels. Under this contract a geopolitical discontinuity of that kind raises Stress and informs Confidence; it does not raise Tail until an observed price path shows sustained mean-reversion failure, and no price path can exist inside the closure. Stress therefore moves from moderate into the elevated band at 46 while Tail stays at 8.

Evidence quality is good for a weekend: current index, futures, volatility, yield and energy levels were verified against primary quote and release pages, the seven-day US calendar was verified against a current calendar source, and the geopolitical development was verified against published reporting. Two limitations are explicit. There is no live price-path evidence, because no venue trades. The shared Finviz context was collected at 02:04Z, is therefore past its ninety-minute freshness bound by the time of this assessment, and reported partial collection with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and independent research carried the assessment. An ADP employment release was omitted from the calendar because its exact date and time for this week could not be verified, and this contract requires omission rather than a guess.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 8 and 22 and never approached the block threshold. The 05:00Z slot on September 25 opened at Tail 18 in normal conditions. The European and US cash stretch from 06:00Z to 14:00Z produced four trend-up prints and a run of WATCH states at Tail 20-22 as the index worked higher, and the 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. From 15:00Z conditions settled back to mixed at Tail 18-19, and the final seven hours fell to Tail 12, 10, 10, 9, 9, 8, 8 and 8 as the Friday settle passed and the weekend closure began. Stress ran between 44 and 58 throughout, consistently above Tail, which is the intended separation: the trailing window contained a difficult high-yield environment, not a pathological price path.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, eighteen hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 10 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or an index pinned near an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Tail eases to 7 through the middle of Saturday, when the reopen is furthest away, then firms to 9 and 10 across Sunday on reopen proximity alone rather than on any observation. Stress traces the mirror path, easing from 46 to 43 through the quietest weekend hours and firming to 50 by the final slot as the reopen and Wednesday's August PCE draw nearer. Confidence decays from 84 to 78 because the newest verified Nasdaq-100 observation keeps ageing with nothing able to replace it. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and the reopen gap itself lies outside this forecast.
